newsitem.title: USA: Interstate Bakeries sees smaller Q4 gains.
newsitem.headline: Interstate Bakeries sees smaller Q4 gains.

text.p: Interstate Bakeries Corp, the largest baker and distributor of fresh branded bread and cake products in the U.S., said Wednesday its fiscal fourth quarter looks strong but financial results are not expected to match the gains of the past three quarters.

Interstate Bakeries is on track for a strong fourth quarter, "though we do not expect the increases to be of the magnitude of the prior three," Charles Sullivan, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
He said priorities for the fourth quarter would be to build unit sales volume in branded bread and cake, and to continue to improve operating margins through further cost containment.
The company reported today that its fiscal third quarter net sales, adjusted to reflect acquisitions and divestitures, rose 4.5 percent from a year earlier, to $945.3 million.
Net income for the quarter, ended March 8, increased more than 400 percent, to $0.59 a share.
Sullivan attributed the gains to continued brand-building efforts and concentration on cost-control measures.

"We are very pleased with our company's results for the quarter. Our net dollar sales and earnings remained strong and exceeded expectations. Unit volume is also responding to our brand-building programs," he said.

"We have exceeded expectations through the first three quarters of our fiscal year," Sullivan said. "We have improved operating margins through operating efficiencies and careful management of expenses, particularly in the area of selling and delivery. That, combined with a recent moderation in ingredient prices, bodes well for the future."
In other developments, IBC introduced three varieties of Wonder Fat-Free bread in an Indianapolis market test. The new line also has been extended to Cincinnati under the Butternut label.
"Initial results are promising, but it's too early to assess product success," Sullivan said.
Shares of Interstate Bakeries were up 1-5/8 to 49-3/8.
